metadata.title: Goldilocks CSLR quantile forest for k-point mesh index (PSDI 52713-55d86)
metadata.description:
A quantile random forest that predicts which mesh a periodic material needs from Goldilocks Core's ordered ladder of k-point meshes. It returns a rung on that ladder, not a k-point spacing: rung 1 is the Gamma-only (1, 1, 1) mesh, indices are 1-based, and the ladder was enumerated down to a minimum k-distance of 0.03 inverse angstrom rather than a fixed count per axis.

Trained on PSDI record 52713-55d86: the same 17757 MC3D structures as the superseded record d5ds2-64f16, relabelled under the corrected floor-based ladder -- not a uniform shift, since the 1-based enumeration also drops a small number of repeated meshes that the old per-axis count did not. Convergence is judged on total energy alone, to within 1 meV/atom across three consecutive rungs; no force criterion is applied. Split 70/10/10/10 and grouped by reduced composition so that polymorphs of one composition cannot straddle the split. Inputs are 174 composition, structure, direct-lattice and reciprocal-lattice descriptors, matching the extractor Goldilocks Core already uses. No SOAP and no learned metallicity representation.

The model publishes a whole rung, not its raw best estimate, but no longer under the 6% under-prediction floor a previous version of this record held. That floor forced a q0.95 level costing almost 3 rungs of extra mesh on every recommendation -- most of the distance between the model and the truth, not a small correction on top of a good estimate. This version publishes q0.6 instead, chosen as the cheapest level that keeps under-prediction below 25% on the validation split. On the held-out test split it is close to unbiased (mean excess +0.06 rungs) and comes in below the true rung 22.9% of the time, against 3.5% and a mean of +2.96 rungs on the superseded policy: the trade is real in both directions, not a free improvement.

Because the published value now sits close to the estimator's own distribution rather than deliberately above it, symmetric error metrics describe the estimator directly: test MAE is 1.13 and R-squared is 0.74. The cost is concentrated exactly where it always was: structures that truly need rung 12 or above are under-converged 76.7% of the time at this level, against 17.8% under the previous, more conservative policy. A prediction for a structure expected to be demanding must be checked against convergence directly, not trusted at face value -- more so under this policy than the one it replaces. 0.6% of the training labels sit at the top of the ladder and the model cannot place them regardless of policy. That limit is stated in the model card rather than smoothed over.

The record contains the fitted forest, its separately recorded calibration, and model.json, which was written by the run that fitted the model and records the feature contract, all 174 column names, the target contract, the decision rule and the rule that chose it, the hyperparameter search, and the digests.
